analytical_models.equation_role: Convert the average kernel average misorientation (θ) into a dislocation density using the EBSD step size (μ) and Burgers vector (b)
analytical_models.model_note: Applied to the high-temperature rolling zone samples (R850, R950).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fixed steel composition (Fe–0.35C–0.26Si–1.47Mn–4.50Al–0.26Cr–0.28Mo–1.47Ni, wt.%) over the temperature range ~500–1500 °C
computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic equilibrium calculation (CALPHAD-type equilibrium phase diagram and phase-fraction vs temperature)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The predicted carbide stability temperature range (<750 °C) is consistent with the experimentally observed decrease in carbide/ferrite composite lamellae fraction from 51.5 % (R650) to 43.3 % (R750) and with the complete dissolution of carbides in the high-temperature rolling zone (R850/R950).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: interfacial stress concentration caused by phase hardness mismatch
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Significant hardness differences between martensite, δ-ferrite and DIF weaken the bonding at phase interfaces and concentrate stress at the crack tip; the maximum hardness difference reaches 3.86 GPa (martensite 5.98–6.50 GPa > DIF 2.84–2.98 GPa > δ-ferrite 2.64–2.77 GPa). These phase boundaries become preferential sites for crack initiation.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack propagation shortcut via pre-existing defects
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The equiaxed ferrite (DIF) grains embedded in the honeycomb martensite act as pre-existing defects / 'crack propagation shortcuts', guiding cracks to propagate rapidly in a cleavage mode and significantly reducing energy consumption; cracks propagate straight through the carbide-free honeycomb structure with no blunting or deflection.

interfaces.interface_notes: Hardness mismatch induces stress concentration at phase boundaries (preferential crack-initiation sites); the high brittleness of the honeycomb martensite lamellae inhibits plastic deformation, and the DIF grains guide cleavage crack propagation, producing typical brittle fracture.
interfaces.phase_evolution: At 950 °C (high-temperature rolling zone) carbides dissolve completely; the temperature lies in the δ + γ two-phase region where austenite stability and carbon solubility are enhanced by austenite-stabilizing elements (e.g. Mn), promoting carbide dissolution. Part of the austenite decomposes into equiaxed ferrite (DIFT) during deformation, and the residual austenite transforms to martensite after rolling, giving equiaxed ferrite grains surrounded by martensite.
interfaces.slip_behavior: The carbide-free R950 shows no Orowan pinning contribution; the work-hardening rate curve decreases monotonically without a hump, indicating a lack of coordinated deformation capacity among the phases and brittle, unstable crack propagation immediately after initiation.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Room-temperature impact absorption energy (IAE), total elongation (TE) and strength-plasticity product (SPP): R950 IAE 4.6 ± 0.2 J vs R650 207.5 ± 29.3 J; TE 3.5 ± 0.8 % vs 19.0 ± 3.2 %; SPP 4.4 ± 1.0 GPa % vs 16.5 ± 1.5 GPa %; UTS increases from 868.7 ± 16.4 MPa (R650) to 1254.5 ± 70.0 MPa (R950).

service_conditions.stress_state: Charpy impact (dynamic) and uniaxial tension along RD, both at room temperature

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Upstream step shared by all rolled specimens (parent process proc_hotforged-ac): steel ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h prior to hot forging.
Hot forged to a plate thickness of 40 mm, then air cooled to room temperature (parent process proc_hotforged-ac).

processing_steps.method: reheating and holding in a box furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The R950 specimen was heated to 950 °C (highest of the four rolling temperatures 650/750/850/950 °C) and held for 2 h before rolling; 950 °C lies in the high-temperature rolling zone (≥850 °C) and within the δ-ferrite + austenite two-phase region.
Rolling deformation with a 60 % reduction ratio, reducing the plate thickness from 40 mm to 16 mm; 60 % deformation ensures full microstructure reconstruction.
After rolling the plate was air cooled to room temperature, giving the R950 condition; residual austenite transforms to martensite during air cooling.

structures.overall_structure: High-temperature-rolled duplex lamellar structure formed by hot rolling at 950 °C: alternating δ-ferrite lamellae (light) and honeycomb martensite lamellae (dark), with numerous equiaxed ferrite grains (deformation-induced ferrite, DIF) enclosed within the honeycomb martensite lamellae. Carbides are completely dissolved, so no carbide/ferrite composite lamellae are present.

defects.lattice_distortion: KAM value decreases to 0.3–0.4° in the high-temperature rolling zone

grain_structure.texture: <101> preferred orientation (shifted from <001>) with large elongated grains indicating grain growth

phases_present.morphology: large elongated grains coloured green, blue and pink in the IPF map, indicating grain growth

structures.overall_structure: EBSD-measured crystallographic characteristics of R950: the highest fraction of high-angle grain boundaries and of grains with GOS ≤ 2° among the four conditions, with a coarse, multi-coloured (equiaxed/elongated) grain structure in the IPF map indicating grain growth and the formation of numerous new grains (recrystallized and DIF).

unmapped_findings: For the high-temperature rolling zone (R850/R950) the phase hardness mismatch follows martensite (5.98–6.50 GPa) > DIF (2.84–2.98 GPa) > δ-ferrite (2.64–2.77 GPa), with a maximum hardness difference reaching 3.86 GPa.

Impact absorption energy of the test steel in the high-temperature rolling zone decreases significantly to <10 J; R950 (4.6 ± 0.2 J) fails by typical brittle fracture with cracks propagating straight through the carbide-free honeycomb structure with no blunting or deflection.

R950 belongs to the high-temperature rolling zone where carbides dissolve completely and the structure transforms into a duplex δ-ferrite lamellae + honeycomb martensite lamellae structure containing equiaxed DIF grains that grow with increasing rolling temperature.

Hardness of each phase in the high-temperature rolling zone exhibits a gradient distribution; the large hardness difference between phases causes stress concentration at phase boundaries, which become preferential sites for crack initiation.

In the R950 condition the equiaxed DIF grains originate from two mechanisms: dynamic recrystallization (new grains with increased HAGB and GOS≤2° fractions and decreased KAM/dislocation density) and deformation-induced ferrite transformation (DIFT) during hot rolling, with DIF having submicron size and higher hardness than recrystallized ferrite.

Abstract-level statement for the high-temperature rolling zone: impact energy less than 7 J at room temperature with elongation less than 9 %, and a monotonically decreasing θ-curve due to phase hardness mismatch (martensite/ferrite hardness difference >3.3 GPa).
